title: APIs
snippet:
There is no static API reference for Twenty. Each workspace has its own schema — when you add a custom object (say `Invoice`), it immediately gets REST and GraphQL endpoints identical to built-in objects like `Company` or `Person`. The API is generated from the schema, so endpoints use your object and field names directly — no opaque IDs. Your workspace-specific API documentation is available under **Settings → Developers → API** after creating an API key.

| Environment | Base URL |
|---|---|
| Cloud | `https://api.twenty.com/` |
| Self-Hosted | `https://{your-domain}/` |
## Authentication
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```
Create an API key in **Settings → Developers → API → + Create key**. Copy it immediately — it’s shown once. Keys can be scoped to a specific role under **Settings → Members → Roles → Assignment tab** to limit what they can access. For OAuth-based access (external apps acting on behalf of users), see [OAuth](/developers/extend/oauth).

title: Pricing Plans
snippet:
[twenty.com/pricing](https://twenty.com/pricing).

## Self-Hosted Plans
### Free (Self-Hosted)
Host Twenty on your own infrastructure at no cost:
- All Pro CRM features, plus custom roles
- AI runs on your own AI provider keys, without personal AI usage or workspace credits
- Community support via Discord
- Full control over your data
### Organization (Self-Hosted)
For teams who need premium features while self-hosting:
- Everything in Free
- **Premium features**: row-level permissions, SSO and more
- Twenty team support
- No requirement to publish custom code as open-source before distributing
Premium features are only available on the Organization plans (Cloud or Self-Hosted):
- **Custom roles**: Roles beyond Admin and Member, with object and field permissions (on Cloud, Pro (Early) keeps them too; self-hosted instances include them on every plan)
- **Row-level permissions**: Fine-grained access control at the record level
- **SSO integration**: Single Sign-On with your identity provider
- **Audit logs**: Check what each workspace member has been doing
- **Usage limits for members, API keys and apps**: Cap what each of them can spend
- **Custom domain**: Serve your workspace from your own domain (also available on self-hosted instances)
- **Unlimited workspaces**: Create as many workspaces as you want (self-hosted only)
- **Private source code**: No requirement to publish changes to a publicly available repository (self-hosted only)

title: twenty/packages/twenty-docs/developers/api-and-webhooks/api.mdx at d05c92ad7bd1b15e36978b2495d6e06fc7bdc8ae · twentyhq/twenty
snippet:
The Twenty API allows developers to interact programmatically with the Twenty CRM platform. Using the API, you can integrate Twenty with other systems, automate data synchronization, and build custom solutions around your customer data. The API provides endpoints to **create, read, update, and delete** core CRM objects (such as people and companies) as well as access metadata configuration.

Twenty’s API uses API keys for authentication. Every request to protected endpoints must include an API key in the header.
- **API Keys:** You can generate a new API key from your Twenty app’s **API settings** page. Each API key is a secret token that grants access to your CRM data, so keep it safe. If a key is compromised, revoke it from the settings and generate a new one.
- **Auth Header:** Once you have an API key, include it in the `Authorization` header of your HTTP requests. Use the Bearer token scheme. For example:
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```
Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with the key you obtained. This header must be present on **all API requests**. If the token is missing or invalid, the API will respond with an authentication error (HTTP 401 Unauthorized).
## API Endpoints
All resources can be accessed and via REST or GraphQL.
- **Cloud:** `https://api.twenty.com/` or your custom domain / sub-domain
- **Self-Hosted Instances:** If you are running Twenty on your own server, use your own domain in place of `api.twenty.com` (for example, `https://{your-domain}/rest/`).

title: OAuth
snippet:
Twenty implements OAuth 2.0 with authorization code + PKCE for user-facing apps and client credentials for server-to-server access. Clients are registered dynamically via [RFC 7591](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591) — no manual setup in a dashboard.

## Scopes
| Scope | Access |
|---|---|
| `api` | Full read/write access to the Core and Metadata APIs |
| `profile` | Read the authenticated user’s profile information |
Request scopes as a space-separated string: `scope=api profile`
